Bayview Hunters Point.title: Shadow O'Clock
Bayview Hunters Point.do: Climb to Hilltop Park and its giant yellow sundial (the shadow-casting arm is 70 feet long). Phones and watches away. Read the time from the sundial, convert it to clock time yourselves (hint: think about daylight saving), and write your answer down. Then check a phone: within 15 minutes = complete. Off by more = wait 10 minutes and read it again. No shadow because of fog? Everyone touches the gnomon at once instead.
Bayview Hunters Point.where: Hilltop Park, Whitney Young Circle at Newcomb Ave.
Bayview Hunters Point.photo: A teammate standing on the shadow line holding up the written time.

Bayview Hunters Point.title: Mural Memory on Third Street
Bayview Hunters Point.do: Find the Tuzuri Watu mural ("We Are Beautiful People," 1987) at Third & Palou. Everyone studies it for 60 seconds, then the whole team turns its back. Three fixed questions, answered as a team: (1) how many human faces are painted, (2) how many of them wear something on their head, (3) what color is the largest figure's clothing. Turn around and check by counting together. Three for three = complete. Any miss = a new 60 seconds and try again.
Bayview Hunters Point.where: Third St & Palou Ave (the Obama mural at Third & Oakdale, two blocks on, works as a second board with the same three questions).
Bayview Hunters Point.photo: Backs to the wall mid-answer, then the recount with fingers on faces.

Bayview Hunters Point.title: Count the Quesada Palms
Bayview Hunters Point.do: Quesada Avenue between Third St and Newhall St has a strip of towering palm trees down its center median, wrapped by the famous Quesada community gardens. Two teammates become the counters: one walks the north sidewalk, one the south, each silently counting every palm trunk in the median. At the Newhall end they say their numbers at the same time. A match = complete. A mismatch = swap sidewalks and count again. (Team of two: you're both counters.)
Bayview Hunters Point.where: Quesada Ave median, Third St to Newhall St
Bayview Hunters Point.photo: Both counters holding up their matching number on fingers at the Newhall end, the palm boulevard behind.

Bernal Heights.title: Cardboard Curling at the Twin Slides
Bernal Heights.do: At Esmeralda Slide Park, every teammate rides the twin 40-foot slides at least once (grab a piece of the cardboard traditionally left at the top, or bring your own). Then the game: mark a target zone at the bottom of one slide — a shoe placed one stride past the slide's lip. Send an EMPTY piece of cardboard down the slide, no rider, no push after release. Complete when a piece comes to rest touching the shoe. Overshoots and stalls are retries; rotate throwers; clear the run-out between goes.
Bernal Heights.where: Esmeralda Slide Park, on the Esmeralda Ave stairway between Winfield St and Prospect Ave (community street park, open daylight hours, free).
Bernal Heights.photo: The cardboard kissing the shoe at the bottom of the slide, the team leaning in like a curling rink.

Bernal Heights.title: I Spy From Sutrito
Bernal Heights.do: Climb to the summit of Bernal Hill (the little radio tower locals call "Sutrito," a mini Sutro Tower) and play I Spy with the whole city as the board. The spy picks anything visible from the top — a tower, a bridge, a hill, a boat, a water tank — and gives the classic clue ("I spy something red and pointy"). Teammates guess by pointing — THREE guesses each per round; the spy says yes or no. Found = the next teammate is the spy. Nobody finds it = the spy reveals, and takes another turn with a new object. Complete when every teammate has been the spy once and had their thing found.
Bernal Heights.where: Bernal Heights Park summit, off Bernal Heights Blvd (open 24/7; the Esmeralda stairway from the slides leads straight up).
Bernal Heights.photo: The team at the summit fence, everyone pointing at the last thing spied, 360° of city behind.

Bernal Heights.title: One Foot on the Steepest Street
Bernal Heights.do: Walk to the top block of Bradford Street above Tompkins Avenue — at a 41% grade, the steepest street in San Francisco (Lombard's crooked block is only 27%). On the sidewalk, every teammate stands on ONE foot, facing downhill, for a fully counted 20 seconds at the same time. Anyone's second foot touches down = everyone restarts the count. Complete on one clean 20.
Bernal Heights.where: Bradford St between Tompkins Ave and Jarboe Ave, east slope of Bernal Hill.
Bernal Heights.photo: The flamingo line on the 41% sidewalk, street sign in frame.

Castro/Upper Market.title: Marquee Recall at the Castro Theatre
Castro/Upper Market.do: Stand across Castro St from the Castro Theatre's giant neon blade sign and marquee. Everyone studies the marquee for exactly 30 seconds — every title, date and showtime on it — then the whole team turns its back. One teammate at a time names ONE item from the marquee; the team keeps a written list. A repeat or anything not on the marquee ends the round. Turn around and check: complete when the list matches every line on the marquee. Short? New 30-second look, list starts over.
Castro/Upper Market.where: Castro Theatre, 429 Castro St (view from the opposite sidewalk).
Castro/Upper Market.photo: The team with their backs to the marquee, the written list held up.

Castro/Upper Market.title: Twenty Questions at Cliff's
Castro/Upper Market.do: Cliff's Variety has sold a bit of everything since 1936. One teammate, the shopper, goes in alone and buys ONE item for $5 or less, then hides it in a bag. The rest of the team gets TWENTY yes-or-no questions to name what it is. Named within twenty = complete. Stumped = new shopper, new item, try again.
Castro/Upper Market.photo: The big reveal: the item pulled from the bag, the team mid-groan or mid-cheer, Cliff's storefront behind.

Castro/Upper Market.title: Walk the Rainbow
Castro/Upper Market.do: At 18th & Castro, the crosswalks are painted in rainbow stripes that run the length of the crossing. Each teammate picks a different color stripe. When the WALK signal comes on, everyone crosses together with both feet staying on their own color the whole way — no stepping onto a neighbor's stripe. Anyone steps off, the whole team turns around and recrosses on the next WALK signal. Complete when the team makes one clean crossing. Cross only on the signal, and keep moving with the crowd.
Castro/Upper Market.where: The rainbow crosswalks at 18th St & Castro St.
Castro/Upper Market.photo: Shot from the curb: the team mid-crossing, one person per stripe, the giant rainbow flag up the block.

Chinatown.title: The Ransom-Note Fortune
Chinatown.do: Buy one bag at the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory. Crack a cookie, tear the fortune into scraps carrying one letter each, and start assembling the phrase SAN FRAN ransom-note style (S, A, A, N, N, F, R — the F is the hard part; plenty of fortunes don't have one). Only letters torn from fortune slips count, each scrap used once. Keep cracking cookies from your bag until you can lay out the full phrase. If an entire bag can't produce it, buy another and reflect on your luck.
Chinatown.where: Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory, 56 Ross Alley (between Washington & Jackson); open daily, until ~7pm weekends
Chinatown.cost: ~$5–8 for the bag (a small photo fee may apply inside)
Chinatown.photo: SAN FRAN assembled from torn destiny on a step in Ross Alley, the pile of sacrificed cookies alongside.

Chinatown.title: The Lamplighter's Census
Chinatown.do: Grant Avenue's cast-iron dragon streetlamps have coiled on their posts since 1925. Stand at the Dragon Gate (Bush & Grant). BEFORE anyone takes a step up Grant, the team locks in ONE written estimate: how many dragon lampposts stand on Grant between the gate and Broadway? No research, no peeking up the street beyond what you can see from the gate. Then walk all eight blocks and count every lamp as a team. Estimate within ±15% of your count = win. You get exactly one estimate, ever.
Chinatown.where: Grant Ave from the Dragon Gate (at Bush) to Broadway
Chinatown.photo: The written estimate held up at the Dragon Gate before the walk, then the final tally beside the last lamp at Broadway.

Chinatown.title: The Hand Knows
Chinatown.do: At any Stockton Street produce market, the buyer picks THREE different fruits — any fruits at all, from the everyday to the unpronounceable — hidden from one blindfolded teammate. The guesser holds each fruit for up to 30 seconds — touch only, no smelling, no tasting, no hints — and names it. Two of three correct = complete. Fewer = retry with three new fruits and a new guesser. Then eat your props.
Chinatown.where: Stockton St between Sacramento St and Broadway (market blocks)
Chinatown.photo: The blindfolded guesser gingerly palming a dragonfruit, market bins spilling behind — then the whole team mid-bite.

Excelsior.title: Paris, France (No Passport Required)
Excelsior.do: The Excelsior's streets are named for world capitals and their avenues for countries. Phones away — no maps. Find a corner where a capital meets its OWN country (Paris St & France Ave, Naples St & Italy Ave, or Moscow St & Russia Ave) and photograph the team under the sign pair. Then find two "scrambled geography" corners (e.g., Paris & Russia, London & Persia) and photograph those sign pairs too.
Excelsior.where: The Excelsior's capitals-and-countries grid, east of Mission St.
Excelsior.photo: The team under PARIS / FRANCE, plus two scrambled-geography sign pairs.

Excelsior.title: Last Supper Charades
Excelsior.do: Go to the 1935 Art Deco Royal Baking Company building, whose facade is painted with a multi-panel "Last Supper" mural — thirteen figures, thirteen poses. Number the figures 1–13 from the left. One teammate, the performer, generates a random number on a phone (re-roll repeats) and freezes in that figure's exact pose (hands, head, lean). The team gets ONE guess at which painted figure it is — point at them. Right = the next teammate performs. Wrong = the performer picks a new figure and the streak restarts. Complete when the team gets three right in a row. Pan dulce from the legacy bakery inside is optional, and recommended.
Excelsior.where: Royal Bakery, 4773 Mission St (between Russia and France Aves). The mural is outdoors; the bakery is open daily, roughly 9am–8pm.
Excelsior.photo: The performer frozen mid-pose beneath the matching painted figure, the team pointing.

Excelsior.title: Land It on the Rainbow
Excelsior.do: At the Athens Avalon Greenspace, the stairway is mosaicked in a color gradient — cool and dark at the bottom, warm and bright at the top. Stand at the bottom step. A teammate calls a color band ("green!"); the thrower tosses a coin or bottle cap underhand and it must come to rest ON that band. Rotate throwers. Complete when the team lands three called bands (any three, not in a row). Pick up every coin afterward.
Excelsior.where: Athens Avalon Greenspace, 800 Avalon Ave at Athens St (four blocks up the hill from Mission via Avalon).
Excelsior.photo: The coin resting on the called band, the gradient climbing behind.

Financial District/South Beach.title: The Blindfold Market
Financial District/South Beach.do: Pick a taster. The taster waits OUTSIDE the Ferry Building, eyes closed, while a teammate goes in and buys one bite-sized edible thing ($10 max) from any shop or Saturday farmers-market stall — no hints, wrapper hidden. Blindfold the taster (hands over eyes works) and feed them one bite. On camera, they declare what they think it is. Then the blindfold comes off and the taster leads the team inside: they must find the exact shop it came from and point at its sign. They get TWO shop guesses. Both wrong = attempt failed; a retry requires a fresh purchase and, if possible, a fresh taster. You may not practice.
Financial District/South Beach.where: Ferry Building Marketplace, foot of Market St at The Embarcadero.
Financial District/South Beach.photo: The blindfolded tasting under the clock tower, then the triumphant point at the shop sign.

Financial District/South Beach.title: Mind the Doors
Financial District/South Beach.do: The F-line's historic streetcars — each one a rescued antique from a different city and decade — stop along The Embarcadero. Go to any F-line platform. You may watch streetcars arrive for as long as you like. Then declare your attempt: the whole team lines up shoulder-to-shoulder where you believe the FRONT DOOR of the next streetcar will be when it stops, and must be in position before the streetcar is visible. No moving once it appears. If any teammate lines up with any part of the open front door, you win. Miss = wait for the next streetcar to try again (they run every ~10 minutes on weekends).
Financial District/South Beach.where: Any F Market & Wharves platform on The Embarcadero (Ferry Building stop is the classic).
Financial District/South Beach.photo: The team flattened in a line on the platform, antique streetcar door gaping open exactly at (or hilariously far from) them.

Financial District/South Beach.title: Heart Detective
Financial District/South Beach.do: Union Square keeps giant painted heart sculptures from the "Hearts in San Francisco" series stationed around the plaza, repainted by new artists each year. One teammate (the artist) slips away and photographs an extreme close-up — a palm-sized detail — of any one heart, any side. The rest of the team sees only that photo, then must find the spot: identify which heart, walk to it, and put a finger on the exact painted detail. First touch is the answer — right spot wins, wrong heart or wrong spot fails the attempt. Retry with a new close-up and a new artist. Artists may not answer questions.
Financial District/South Beach.photo: Side-by-side keeper: the mystery close-up next to the finger-on-the-spot reveal, Dewey Monument in the background.

Golden Gate Park.title: Spin at the Dutch Windmill
Golden Gate Park.do: Walk to the 75-foot Dutch Windmill at the park's ocean corner. Build a pinwheel from what you have (paper folded and pinned to a pencil or stick; bring a pin or a paperclip) and hold it up in the sea wind in front of the real windmill. Complete when your pinwheel spins on its own for 10 counted seconds without a hand touching the blades.
Golden Gate Park.where: Dutch Windmill / Queen Wilhelmina Garden, northwest corner of the park at John F. Kennedy Dr & the Great Highway
Golden Gate Park.photo: The spinning paper pinwheel with the real sails behind it, tulips in season.

Golden Gate Park.title: Petal Match in the Secret Garden
Golden Gate Park.do: Slip through the wrought-iron gate of the Shakespeare Garden — every plant in it is mentioned in Shakespeare's works. On the brick wall at the back are bronze plaques quoting his flower lines. Pick any flower NAMED on a plaque (violet, rose, daisy, thyme...), then hunt through the beds until you find that flower actually growing. Photograph both: the plaque line and the living plant.
Golden Gate Park.where: Shakespeare Garden, off Martin Luther King Jr. Dr next to the California Academy of Sciences (Music Concourse area, mid-park near 9th Ave)
Golden Gate Park.photo: One teammate pointing at the flower's name on the bronze plaque, another holding a phone/finger next to the real flower.

Golden Gate Park.title: B Is for Bison
Golden Gate Park.do: Yes, there are real bison in San Francisco. Two teammates become the counters: they walk to different spots along the paddock fence (at least 50 paces apart) and silently count every bison they can see — the herd wanders and hides behind hillocks and each other, so it's harder than it sounds. They walk back and say their numbers at the same time. A match = complete. A mismatch = the herd's moved; pick new spots and count again. (Team of two: you're both counters.)
Golden Gate Park.where: Bison Paddock, along John F. Kennedy Dr just west of Spreckels Lake (west end of the park, near 39th Ave; the dirt path along the north side gets you closest)
Golden Gate Park.photo: The two counters holding up matching finger-counts with bison grazing behind them.

Glen Park.title: Leaf Boat Race on Islais Creek
Glen Park.do: Walk the Gum Tree Girls Trail into the canyon floor to the wooden boardwalk where Islais Creek runs through the willows. Each teammate picks a fallen eucalyptus ("gum tree") leaf as their boat. Launch them together from the upstream side of the boardwalk; complete when any leaf floats ten feet downstream without snagging. Snagged fleet = new leaves, new launch. Stay on the boardwalk and the path.
Glen Park.where: Glen Canyon Park — Gum Tree Girls Trail (starts behind the rec center) to the creekside boardwalk
Glen Park.photo: Leaves mid-voyage, the team cheering from the boardwalk.

Glen Park.title: Telephone Up Harry Street
Glen Park.do: Harry Street is one of the last wooden street-staircases in San Francisco — roughly 240 steps climbing a hidden green tunnel between houses, marked only by tiny "Harry" street signs at each end. Play telephone up it: the team spreads out along the stairs, at least ten steps between each person. The bottom teammate writes down a made-up sentence of at least eight words, then whispers it once to the next person up; they whisper it once to the next; and so on to the top. The top teammate says it out loud and the bottom one reveals the paper. Word-for-word match = complete. Anything garbled = new sentence, and everyone shuffles up one position. Then finish the climb to the rocky summit of Billy Goat Hill above Beacon St.
Glen Park.where: Harry Street steps (Laidley St near Harper St, up to Beacon St), then Billy Goat Hill summit
Glen Park.photo: The team strung up the wooden stairs mid-whisper, then the paper held up at Billy Goat Hill with the skyline behind.

Glen Park.title: Recite the Line at Glen Park BART
Glen Park.do: Glen Park's 1973 BART station — raw board-formed concrete and rusting Corten steel — is routinely named one of the finest Brutalist transit buildings in America. Inside, find the system map. One teammate studies it for 60 seconds, then turns away and recites every station from Glen Park to Embarcadero, in order, from memory. The team checks against the map. Any slip = new 60 seconds, new reciter. Complete on a clean run. (No fare needed — the map is outside the gates.)
Glen Park.where: Glen Park BART station, Diamond St & Bosworth St
Glen Park.photo: The reciter with their back to the map, mid-list, concrete overhead.

Haight Ashbury.title: Five-Word Cover at Amoeba
Haight Ashbury.do: Inside Amoeba Music (1855 Haight St, a converted bowling alley), one teammate — the describer — picks any single record from one bin section (the records between two divider cards), memorizes its cover, and slides it back. The describer then tells the team which section it's in and describes the cover in EXACTLY five words — no artist names, no titles, no words printed on the sleeve. The team flips through that section and must hold up the record on their first pick. Right = the next teammate describes. Wrong = new record, streak restarts. Complete when the team gets three in a row. Reshelve everything nicely; no purchase required.
Haight Ashbury.where: Amoeba Music, 1855 Haight St at Stanyan. Open daily 11am–7pm.
Haight Ashbury.cost: $0 (optional: grab something from the bargain bin)
Haight Ashbury.photo: The found record held up next to the describer's five words typed on a phone, bins stretching away behind.

Haight Ashbury.title: Tombstone Gutter Hunt
Haight Ashbury.do: In Buena Vista Park, the paved path gutters are built from broken marble headstones taken from SF's demolished Gold Rush-era cemeteries in the 1930s — most were laid face-down, but some engraving still shows. Walk the paths (the stretch above the tennis courts on the Buena Vista Ave West side is the jackpot zone) and find a gutter fragment with legible carved letters or numbers. Complete with a close-up photo of the engraving with a teammate's finger pointing at it.
Haight Ashbury.where: Buena Vista Park; enter at Haight St & Buena Vista Ave East, or from Buena Vista Ave West near Central Ave for the tennis-court paths.
Haight Ashbury.photo: A finger pointing at 100-plus-year-old tombstone lettering hiding in plain sight in a park gutter.

Haight Ashbury.title: Which House Was the Band's?
Haight Ashbury.do: Somewhere on the 700 block of Ashbury St (between Waller and Frederick) is the Victorian where the Grateful Dead lived in 1966–68. Phones away, no numbers read aloud, and NO TALKING from the moment you turn onto the block. Walk it once in silence, then every teammate secretly writes down which house they think it is — by color and position ("the purple one, third from Waller on the left"). Reveal: if everyone picked the SAME house, complete, whether or not you were right. Split decision = failed — one vote only. Either way, check the number (it's 710) for bragging rights. Private homes — stay on the sidewalk, keep it quiet.
Haight Ashbury.where: Ashbury St between Waller and Frederick, one block uphill from the Haight/Ashbury corner.
Haight Ashbury.photo: The ballots held up in front of the house the team agreed on.

Hayes Valley.title: Painted Lady Charades
Hayes Valley.do: At Alamo Square, face Postcard Row — the seven Painted Ladies of 710–720 Steiner. One teammate, the performer, secretly picks one of the seven at random (a random number 1–7 on a phone, counting from the left). Without words, letters or pointing, the performer acts out THAT house — its color, its trim, its windows, its shape, whatever they can mime. When a teammate thinks they've got it, they cross Steiner and touch that house's front gate or railing (sidewalk only — these are private homes, stay off the steps). Right house = complete. Wrong house = the performer draws a new number and starts over.
Hayes Valley.where: Alamo Square Park, east slope along Steiner St (between Hayes & Fulton). Open daily, dawn to midnight.
Hayes Valley.photo: The guesser's hand on the right gate, the performer mid-mime on the grass across the street, Postcard Row behind.

Hayes Valley.title: A Quarter Pound, By Feel
Hayes Valley.do: At Miette, the pastel patisserie on Octavia whose back wall is jars of bulk candy sold by weight, the team fills ONE bag from the jars trying to land on exactly a quarter pound (4 oz) — no scale, no phone, just hands and arguments. Lock the bag, then let the counter weigh it. Within a quarter ounce (3.75–4.25 oz) = complete. Off? Buy it anyway (that's the evidence, and it's candy), and fill a new bag, wiser. Budget cap $10 across all attempts.
Hayes Valley.where: Miette Patisserie & Confiserie, 449 Octavia St at Linden (open daily, weekend daytime included).
Hayes Valley.photo: The scale readout beside the bag, team faces either way.

Hayes Valley.title: Be the Art
Hayes Valley.do: Find the current rotating installation at the center of Patricia's Green (the Arts Commission swaps it roughly yearly). One teammate, the director, studies it; everyone else keeps their backs to it. Using words only — no gestures — the director arranges the team into a human copy of the sculpture. When the director calls "done," take the photo with sculpture and copy side by side. One rebuild allowed.
Hayes Valley.where: Patricia's Green, Octavia Blvd between Hayes & Fell.
Hayes Valley.photo: The sculpture beside its blind-built human twin.

Inner Richmond.title: The Chopstick Gauntlet
Inner Richmond.do: Join the line at Good Luck Dim Sum, fill out one of the famous pink order sheets, and buy at least 3 DIFFERENT dim sum items for under $10 total — cash only, so have bills ready. Then the gauntlet: on the sidewalk, every teammate must pick up one piece from the box with chopsticks and get it to their mouth — no fingers, no stabbing, no two-handed chopsticks. A drop means that teammate takes another piece and tries again. Complete when every teammate has landed one clean bite. (Chopsticks come in the bag; ask for extras.)
Inner Richmond.where: Good Luck Dim Sum, 736 Clement St (between 8th & 9th Ave); open Sat–Sun 8:00am–4:30pm
Inner Richmond.time: 15 min (the line is part of the legend)
Inner Richmond.photo: A teammate mid-lift, dumpling wobbling in the chopsticks, pink box open, Clement Street behind.

Inner Richmond.title: Spell Your Colors
Inner Richmond.do: Inside Green Apple Books (est. 1967, creaky floors included), pull used books whose titles' FIRST letters spell your team's color — R-E-D or B-L-U-E — one book per letter, in order. Stack or fan the spines so the letters read top to bottom. Reshelve everything afterward. Complete when the photo clearly shows the spines spelling your color.
Inner Richmond.where: Green Apple Books, 506 Clement St at 6th Ave; open daily, weekend daytime included
Inner Richmond.time: 10–15 min (Blue teams earn their extra letter)
Inner Richmond.photo: The stacked spines spelling RED or BLUE, taken in the maze of used-book shelves.

Inner Richmond.title: Creature Checklist at the Fish Emporium
Inner Richmond.do: Browse the 6th Ave Aquarium, the cavernous fish store stacked floor to ceiling with tanks. Photograph all three of: (a) a koi, (b) a crab or lobster or shrimp, and (c) a fish longer than your hand (hand in frame next to the tank for scale). Look only — no tapping on glass. Complete when you have all three shots.
Inner Richmond.where: 6th Ave Aquarium, 425 Clement St (between 5th & 6th Ave); open weekend daytime from mid-morning
Inner Richmond.photo: The hand-for-scale shot next to the biggest fish you found.

Inner Sunset.title: Spot the Teammate from Turtle Hill
Inner Sunset.do: Split up at 14th Ave & Moraga. One teammate, the runner, generates two random numbers on a phone — a direction (1 north, 2 south, 3 east, 4 west) and a distance (1–3 blocks) — walks to that corner and stands still on the sidewalk: no waving, no bright jacket held up, no texting. The rest climb the wooden stairs to the bare-sand summit of Grandview Park ("Turtle Hill") and must find the runner: they text the corner they think the runner is on. Right corner = complete. Wrong = the runner texts "no" — three wrong texts and the runner re-rolls a new corner while the spotters look away. (Runner: if your corner isn't visible from the summit, re-roll before the others reach the top.)
Inner Sunset.where: Grandview Park, stairs from 14th Ave & Moraga to the summit
Inner Sunset.photo: The zoomed find — a tiny teammate on a distant corner — and the summit crew pointing.

Inner Sunset.title: Orange Tiles Only
Inner Sunset.do: At the Hidden Garden Steps (148 mosaic risers), find the giant orange salamander that snakes up 26 of the steps. Every teammate climbs the salamander's stretch stepping ONLY where the orange of its body meets the step — never on the blue-and-green background tiles. Foot on the background = back to the salamander's tail. Complete when everyone has done a clean climb.
Inner Sunset.where: Hidden Garden Steps, 16th Ave between Kirkham and Lawton
Inner Sunset.photo: A foot mid-step on the orange, the salamander curling up the stairs.

Inner Sunset.title: First-Take Magic
Inner Sunset.do: Enter Misdirections Magic Shop — San Francisco's last brick-and-mortar magic shop — and have one teammate, the magician, buy any beginner trick for $10 or less (teammates wait outside). The magician practices out of sight as long as they like, then announces "official take" and performs it once for the team on video. Complete if the trick WORKS on that take — the coin vanishes, the card is found, the rope is restored — with no visible flub. Flubbed? More practice, and another official take.
Inner Sunset.where: Misdirections Magic Shop, 1236 9th Ave (between Lincoln & Irving); open weekend daytime.
Inner Sunset.photo: The reveal, mid-gasp, with the shop's storefront behind.

Japantown.title: Crane Landing
Japantown.do: Buy origami paper at Paper Tree — The Origami Store (family-run here since 1968). Pick a folder and a reader. The reader looks at a crane diagram (or phone tutorial); the folder may NOT look at it and must fold only from the reader's spoken instructions — no pointing, no touching the paper. When the crane is done, perch it on the low stone wall of one of Ruth Asawa's bronze Origami Fountains on the Buchanan Mall. A torn or failed crane = fresh sheet, try again.
Japantown.where: Paper Tree, 1743 Buchanan St, then the Buchanan Mall fountains.
Japantown.photo: The talked-through crane perched on Asawa's bronze origami fountain.

Japantown.title: Eat Something With a Face
Japantown.do: In the Japan Center malls' food corridors, buy one snack or dessert shaped like an animal — a taiyaki fish cone at Uji Time, a fish waffle, a panda bun, anything with a recognizable creature form — and photograph a teammate taking a bite while the animal is still clearly identifiable. Complete on purchase + photo.
Japantown.where: Japan Center malls, Post St between Fillmore & Laguna (e.g. Uji Time, 22 Peace Plaza #440; malls are liveliest on weekend afternoons).
Japantown.photo: Mid-chomp portrait — teammate vs. fish (or panda), face to face.

Japantown.title: Call Your Capsule
Japantown.do: At the Gashapon Bandai Official Shop (or any capsule-machine bank in the Japan Center malls), pick one machine. Before turning the crank, record a short video of a teammate declaring the color of the capsule shell that will come out (most machines mix 4–5 shell colors). One turn only: if the capsule matches the called color, the challenge is complete; if not, it's failed — but you keep the mystery toy either way.
Japantown.where: Gashapon Bandai Official Shop, Japan Center (Kinokuniya Building, 1581 Webster St); other capsule banks throughout both malls also count.
Japantown.photo: The opened capsule half held next to the toy, machine wall behind — plus the declaration video.

Lakeshore.title: Dune Pictionary at the Glider Deck
Lakeshore.do: From the Fort Funston main parking lot, walk to the wooden hang glider viewing deck at the cliff edge, then step onto the open sand beside it. Play Pictionary in the dune: one teammate, the artist, generates a random number 1–8 on a phone and draws that item from this list — 1 dog, 2 hang glider, 3 wave, 4 bunker, 5 gull, 6 surfer, 7 lighthouse, 8 crab — in the sand with a finger or stick (re-roll repeats). No letters, no numbers, no talking. The team gets three guesses. Right = the next teammate draws. Wrong = smooth the sand, new artist, streak restarts. Complete when three drawings in a row are guessed. Stay behind the fence line — the cliff is real.
Lakeshore.where: Fort Funston, end of Fort Funston Rd off Skyline Blvd; the deck and dunes are beside the main lot.
Lakeshore.photo: The winning sand drawing with the artist's finger still in it, hang gliders (if you're lucky) over the deck behind.

Lakeshore.title: Anza by Touch
Lakeshore.do: Find the bronze equestrian statue of Juan Bautista de Anza (founder of San Francisco, exiled here from Justin Herman Plaza in 2003) on the lake's north shore. One teammate closes their eyes and is led to the statue's base. The three parts to find by touch alone are fixed: a stirrup, the sword's hilt, and the horse's tail. The blind teammate must lay a hand on each, in any order, with no guidance. Three for three = complete. A miss = new blind teammate.
Lakeshore.where: Lakeside pullout/parking area off Lake Merced Blvd at the north end of Lake Merced — the horse is visible from the road.
Lakeshore.photo: Eyes shut, hand on the hoof, the founder of San Francisco looming above.

Lakeshore.title: Claw Patrol
Lakeshore.do: Descend into Round1, the giant arcade in Stonestown's former Nordstrom basement, and win any physical prize from a claw machine. Budget cap: $5 of credits. Prize in hand = complete; $5 gone with empty hands = failed.
Lakeshore.where: Round1 Bowling & Arcade, 285 Winston Dr (lower level, Stonestown Galleria). Open weekends 10am–2am.
Lakeshore.photo: The winner hoisting the prize in front of the wall of claw machines.

Lincoln Park.title: Ships in the Gate
Lincoln Park.do: From the Eagle's Point overlook at the east end of the Coastal Trail, the Golden Gate is dead ahead. Before anyone starts watching the water, the team agrees on ONE guess: how many vessels of any size — freighters, ferries, sailboats, kayaks — will pass through the Gate (under or in line with the bridge) in the next TEN minutes? Write it down, start the clock, and count together. Within 1 of the true count = complete. Off? Call the next ten minutes.
Lincoln Park.where: Eagle's Point overlook, Coastal Trail trailhead at 32nd Ave & El Camino del Mar (a five-minute walk from the Legion of Honor)
Lincoln Park.photo: The guess and the tally held up with the bridge and a passing ship behind.

Lincoln Park.title: See the Ocean Through a Battle Scar
Lincoln Park.do: At the USS San Francisco Memorial, you're standing at the real bridge wings of the cruiser USS San Francisco, riddled with shell holes from the night Battle of Guadalcanal (Nov 1942). Two finds to complete: (a) locate a hole punched clean through the steel and photograph the Pacific or sky visible through it; (b) on the memorial's bronze plaques, find and photograph the name of Admiral Daniel J. Callaghan, who was lost on that bridge and received the Medal of Honor. Bonus fact for the car ride: the memorial is aimed along the exact compass course from San Francisco to Guadalcanal.
Lincoln Park.where: USS San Francisco Memorial overlook, 2400 El Camino del Mar (west end, by the flagpole at the Lands End parking loop above the Coastal Trail).
Lincoln Park.photo: The ocean framed inside a jagged shell hole in the gray steel — plus the close-up of Callaghan's name.

Lincoln Park.title: Walk the Vanishing Labyrinth
Lincoln Park.do: From the Eagle's Point end of the Coastal Trail, take the signed spur path down toward Lands End Point — the rocky promontory with the Golden Gate Bridge dead ahead. Completion: the whole team reaches the flat clearing at the point. If the famous stone labyrinth is standing (artist Eduardo Aguilera first laid it in 2004; vandals keep scattering it and volunteers keep rebuilding it — it was back as of 2025), one teammate must walk the full spiral to the center without cutting across the lines and pose there. Go slowly on the narrow spur, and skip the outermost rocks if it's wet.
Lincoln Park.where: Lands End Point spur, off the Coastal Trail just west of the Eagle's Point overlook (trail access at El Camino del Mar & 32nd Ave).
Lincoln Park.photo: Team at the point — in the labyrinth's center if it exists that day — with the Golden Gate Bridge behind.

Marina.title: Masterpiece, One Guess
Marina.do: The Palace of Fine Arts is an art thing — so make art. One teammate, the artist, secretly picks a famous painting (one they believe the whole team has seen). Anywhere on the Palace grounds, the artist recreates it by any means: drawn with bought supplies (up to $10), scratched in dirt, arranged from leaves and sticks, or built as a living tableau with the colonnade as backdrop. When the artist says "done," the rest of the team gets ONE collective guess at the painting's name. Right = complete. Wrong = failed. One shot.
Marina.where: Palace of Fine Arts grounds, 3601 Lyon St — lagoon lawn, colonnade, or rotunda.
Marina.photo: The recreation side by side with the artist's reveal of the real painting on their phone, rotunda behind.

Marina.title: Play the Bay's Pipe Organ
Marina.do: Walk the jetty at the end of Yacht Rd (past the St. Francis and Golden Gate yacht clubs) to the Wave Organ, the 1986 acoustic sculpture of 25 pipes played by the tides. Record a video that clearly captures the organ's sound — the gurgles, slaps and hums of the water in the pipes — with a teammate's ear at the pipe in frame. Too faint to hear on playback? Try another pipe, or wait: the organ is loudest near high tide.
Marina.where: Wave Organ, end of the yacht-harbor jetty, Yacht Rd off Marina Blvd (open-air, 24/7).
Marina.photo: The video is the proof — the bay's own music, with your team listening in.

Marina.title: Bridge, Rock, and Boat
Marina.do: From anywhere along the Marina Green waterfront, capture ONE photo that contains all three: the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz Island, and a sailboat with its sail up. All three must be identifiable in a single frame (no stitching).
Marina.where: Marina Green promenade, Marina Blvd between Scott and Webster.
Marina.photo: The trophy shot itself — bridge, prison island, and sail in one frame.

McLaren Park.title: Muse Hunt on Philosopher's Way
McLaren Park.do: Philosopher's Way is a 2.7-mile loop dotted with granite "musing station" plaques. Find TWO different musing stations. At each, one teammate reads the quote aloud ONCE; then a different teammate, without looking, must recite it back word for word. Any slip = read it again and retry. Complete when both quotes have been recited back cleanly.
McLaren Park.where: Philosopher's Way, starting from the Overlook lot at Mansell St & Visitacion Ave.
McLaren Park.photo: The reciter at the granite plaque, eyes closed, mid-quote.

McLaren Park.title: One Hearing at the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater
McLaren Park.do: Go to the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater, the Greek-style bowl named for the Grateful Dead guitarist who grew up in the Excelsior next door. One teammate stands center stage; another sits in the LAST row with a pen. The stage teammate generates eight random words on a phone (search "random word generator"), then reads them aloud ONCE, in order, at any volume — no repeats, no spelling. The back-row teammate writes down what they heard. All eight words, in order = complete. Miss = swap roles, eight new words. (If an actual event is underway, come back later.)
McLaren Park.where: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater, 40 John F. Shelley Dr, mid-park.
McLaren Park.photo: Shot from the back row: the tiny speaker center stage, then the two matching lists held up together.

McLaren Park.title: Slide Squad at Redwood Grove
McLaren Park.do: At the Redwood Grove Playground, every single teammate climbs the multi-tiered log-and-rope tower and rides the 20-foot stainless tube slide from the top. Complete when the last teammate pops out the bottom.
McLaren Park.where: Redwood Grove Playground, off John F. Shelley Dr at the group picnic area on the park's west side.
McLaren Park.photo: The final rider emerging feet-first from the tube with the rest of the team arranged around the exit, cheering.

Mission Bay.title: Trapped in the Infinity Mirror
Mission Bay.do: At Seeing Spheres — the ring of five 15.5-foot mirrored steel spheres on the Chase Center east plaza — take ONE photo in which every teammate's face is visible in a single sphere's mirror, including the photographer (it's a mirror shot, so the camera-holder appears too). Complete when one photo shows the whole team reflected.
Mission Bay.where: Thrive City plaza, east entrance of Chase Center (Terry A. Francois Blvd at Warriors Way).
Mission Bay.photo: The whole team inside one giant mirror, ringed by LED lights, with the other spheres reflecting to infinity behind them.

Mission Bay.title: Bronze Age Charades
Mission Bay.do: Oracle Park is ringed by five Giants legends in bronze: Willie Mays (3rd & King main entrance), Orlando Cepeda and Gaylord Perry (facing each other at 2nd & King), Juan Marichal mid-leg-kick (Lefty O'Doul Plaza, by the 3rd St bridge), and Willie McCovey (China Basin Park, across the cove). Walk the statues and study their poses as long as you like. Then one teammate — the performer — secretly puts all five names in a random order (shuffle them on paper or a phone). Without words, the performer acts out each statue's pose in that order, and the rest of the team names each one. Any wrong guess = the performer reshuffles and starts over from the first statue. Complete when the team names all five in a row.
Mission Bay.where: Oracle Park perimeter, 2nd & King to 3rd & King, plus China Basin Park; perform anywhere along the way (Willie Mays Plaza is the classic stage).
Mission Bay.photo: The performer frozen mid-Marichal-leg-kick in front of a bronze, team pointing and shouting the answer.

Mission Bay.title: Creek Patrol
Mission Bay.do: Walk the public Mission Creek Park path on the south bank of Mission Creek (between the 4th St and 6th St bridges) and get ONE photo with at least TWO wild birds in the same frame, on or over the creek (heron, egret, cormorant, pelican, duck and gull all count — the creek is a bird highway). Complete when you have the shot.
Mission Bay.where: Mission Creek Park path, south bank of the channel, Channel St between 4th and 6th.
Mission Bay.photo: Two birds sharing one frame over the last surviving sliver of the old bay.

Mission.title: Pose Detective
Mission.do: In Clarion Alley, one teammate — the performer — secretly picks any human figure painted in any mural, then walks to the alley entrance and freezes in that figure's pose. The rest of the team walks the alley and must point at the right figure. Two guesses total. Right = complete. Two misses = new performer, new figure, try again.
Mission.where: Clarion Alley, between Mission St and Valencia St (parallel to 17th & 18th).
Mission.photo: Performer and mural figure side by side, identical, with the team pointing.

Mission.title: Balmy Alley Bestiary
Mission.do: Walk Balmy Alley and photograph SIX different animals painted in the murals. No two animals from the same mural. Complete at six.
Mission.where: Balmy Alley, between 24th St and 25th St (parallel to Treat & Harrison).
Mission.photo: Six shots, each a painted animal with a team finger pointing at it.

Mission.title: Concha on the Serpent's Back
Mission.do: Buy one concha at a 24th Street panadería. The carrier balances the paper bag on their head and walks it two blocks to the 24th & York Mini Park — no hands. Drop it = walk back to the bakery door and restart. Deliver it to the giant mosaic Quetzalcoatl serpent and share it astride the serpent.
Mission.where: La Reyna Bakery, 3114 24th St (or Panadería La Mejor, 3329 24th St) to the 24th & York Mini Park.
Mission.photo: Team lined up on the tiled feathered serpent, concha held seashell-side out.

Nob Hill.title: The Clockless Labyrinth
Nob Hill.do: Grace Cathedral's outdoor labyrinth is open 24/7. Pick two walkers and one hidden timekeeper; the walkers give up every phone and watch. Walker one walks the labyrinth entrance to center — no shortcuts, step off the line and that walk restarts — while the timekeeper secretly times it. Then walker two walks it, trying to MATCH walker one's time by feel alone (they may watch walk one; no counting out loud, no signals from anyone). Times within 20 SECONDS of each other = complete. Wider = 10-minute cooldown, then a fresh pair of walks.
Nob Hill.where: Grace Cathedral's outdoor plaza, 1100 California St at Taylor
Nob Hill.photo: Both walkers in the center rosette, the two secret times revealed side by side, cathedral behind.

Nob Hill.title: Call the Crossing
Nob Hill.do: Go to California & Powell — where the California line's tracks cross the Powell lines' tracks beneath a little signal tower. Before any cable car is in sight, record a short video declaring your call: "POWELL" or "CALIFORNIA." The next cable car to enter the intersection decides it — match and you win. Miss? Make a new call (again before the next car appears) and keep playing until the crossing proves you right.
Nob Hill.where: Corner of California St & Powell St (stay on the sidewalk by the signal tower).
Nob Hill.time: 5–20 min (cars run every few minutes on weekends)
Nob Hill.photo: The winning cable car rolling through the crossing, signal tower in view, the team mid-cheer.

Nob Hill.title: The Giant Donut of Polk Street
Nob Hill.do: Go to Bob's Donuts (open 24/7 since forever) and buy ONE giant donut — the dinner-plate-sized one from the case. Photograph a teammate holding it up like a porthole with their face in the hole, under the Bob's neon sign. Then the team must finish the entire donut before leaving the block. Done when it's gone.
Nob Hill.where: Bob's Donuts, 1621 Polk St (between Sacramento & Clay).
Nob Hill.photo: Face framed in the giant donut hole beneath the vintage neon sign.

Noe Valley.title: Spell CLIPPER
Noe Valley.do: Noe Valley is home to Clipper Street — the game's namesake. Walk 24th Street and photograph the letters C, L, I, P, P, E, R, IN ORDER, each from a DIFFERENT sign, storefront, or poster (one letter per sign; the two P's must come from two different signs). Finish with the team under the Clipper Street sign at Clipper & Noe.
Noe Valley.where: 24th St between Church and Diamond, then Clipper St & Noe St.
Noe Valley.photo: The seven letter shots as a strip, plus the team saluting under the CLIPPER street sign.

Noe Valley.title: Unanimous on the 31% Leg-Burner
Noe Valley.do: Walk up the single block of 22nd Street from Church Street to Vicksburg Street — at roughly 31.5% grade it's tied for the steepest street block in San Francisco, so steep the sidewalks are staircases. Every teammate counts the sidewalk steps silently on the way up. At the Vicksburg end, everyone says their number at the same instant. All match = complete. Any disagreement = count again on the way down, then say your numbers at the bottom.
Noe Valley.where: 22nd St between Church St and Vicksburg St
Noe Valley.photo: Everyone holding up the matching number at the top, the staircase-sidewalk dropping away behind.

Noe Valley.title: Tin Hunt at Chocolate Covered
Noe Valley.do: Inside Chocolate Covered (a tiny shop lined floor-to-ceiling with thousands of handmade tins printed with San Francisco street signs, plus 1,000+ chocolate bars from around the world), find and photograph a tin showing any street that crosses 24th Street in Noe Valley (Church, Sanchez, Noe, Castro, Vicksburg, Diamond, Hoffman...). Extra glory — but not required — if you find a CLIPPER tin. Then buy one chocolate bar made in a country no teammate has ever visited. Complete when you have the tin photo and the bar receipt/bar in hand.
Noe Valley.where: Chocolate Covered, 4069 24th St (between Noe & Castro). Open daily 10:30am–6:30pm.
Noe Valley.photo: A teammate holding the street-sign tin next to the far-flung chocolate bar, with the wall of tins behind.

North Beach.title: Sal's Orchestra
North Beach.do: The Musée Mécanique (free entry) holds 300+ antique coin-operated machines, announced by Laffing Sal, the cackling 1930s funhouse giantess. Your task: with at most $3 in quarters per attempt, get THREE machines visibly running AT THE SAME TIME, captured in one continuous video pan — teammates fan out, coins drop in sequence, timing is everything (most machines run well under a minute). Sal counts as a machine. Blow the budget with no triple = attempt over; change machine is on site, try again.
North Beach.where: Musée Mécanique, Pier 45 Shed A, foot of Taylor St (weekends 10am–8pm)
North Beach.photo: Frame-grab of the triple: three antique machines mid-whir in one shot, conductor's arms raised.

North Beach.title: The K-Dock Accord
North Beach.do: At Pier 39's K-Dock, the sea lions have squatted rent-free since 1989. Pick two counters. Standing apart at the rail, each silently counts every sea lion hauled out on the floats — no talking, no pointing, no comparing, up to three minutes each. Both write their number down hidden, then reveal at the same moment. The two counts must MATCH EXACTLY. They do = complete. They don't = failed. One try, ever.
North Beach.where: Pier 39, west side marina (K-Dock viewing area — free, 24/7)
North Beach.photo: The simultaneous reveal — two hands, two numbers, and the raft of judges lounging behind (matching or heartbreakingly off by one).

North Beach.title: Get to Coit Tower
North Beach.do: Get to Coit Tower. That's it — the hill is the challenge. Any route counts: the wooden Filbert Steps through the Grace Marchant Garden (recommended, and listen for the wild parrots), the Greenwich Steps, or the road if you must. Complete when the whole team stands at the tower's base.
North Beach.where: Coit Tower, 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, atop Telegraph Hill
North Beach.photo: The team at the tower's fluted base, city and bay falling away behind.

Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.title: Parked Cars on the Ghost Track
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.do: Urbano Drive is an oval because it sits exactly on the old Ingleside Racetrack, the last horse-racing venue in San Francisco. At the Entrada Court entrance, before anyone looks down the street, the team agrees on ONE guess: how many cars are parked along the OUTER curb of the whole oval right now? Write it down, then walk the full lap counting together. Within 10% = complete. Off? One more guess — the inner curb — and walk the lap again (about a mile). Miss twice = failed.
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.where: Urbano Drive oval, Ingleside Terraces; start and finish at the Entrada Court entrance (Sundial Park is inside it).
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.photo: The guess and the count held up at the Entrada Court gate, the curve of the old track behind.

Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.title: Streetcar Under the Deco Tower
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.do: The El Rey Theater at 1970 Ocean Ave is an Art Deco movie palace with a stepped 150-foot tower (a city landmark; the tower once carried an aircraft beacon). The K Ingleside streetcar runs right down Ocean Avenue in front of it. Capture ONE photo that contains both the full El Rey tower (top included) and a K streetcar passing. Trains come every 10–15 minutes on weekends, so scout your camera angle while you wait. Shoot from the sidewalk — never from the trackway.
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.where: El Rey Theater, 1970 Ocean Ave (at Fairfield Way)
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.photo: the shot itself — streetcar and 150-foot Deco tower in a single frame, team optional in foreground

Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.title: Build a Sundial on the Sundial
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.do: Outside the fence of Sundial Park's giant dial, build your own: a stick or pencil stood upright in the grass or a dirt patch, a ring of pebbles for hour marks. Set it so it reads the CURRENT time within 30 minutes — no compass apps, no peeking at the big dial for the shadow angle. Check against a phone. Complete when it reads right. Fog? Build a pebble cairn instead: seven stones stacked, standing for ten counted seconds.
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.where: Sundial Park lawn, Entrada Court, Ingleside Terraces
Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside.photo: Your six-inch sundial with the 33-foot one behind it, both casting shadows.

Outer Mission.title: Sculpture Safari in the Secret Forest
Outer Mission.do: In Cayuga Park, find and photograph FIVE different hand-carved wooden sculptures by Demetrio Braceros — at least one animal and at least one person among them (he carved everyone from Adam and Eve to John Lennon).
Outer Mission.where: Cayuga Park, Cayuga Ave at Naglee Ave.
Outer Mission.photo: Five carving shots; the keeper is a teammate beside their favorite.

Outer Mission.title: Call the Cars
Outer Mission.do: Stand in Cayuga Park directly under the elevated BART tracks. Before each train, the team agrees on ONE call: how many cars will the next train have? (BART runs trains of different lengths.) Say it out loud on video, then count the cars as they thunder overhead. Exactly right = complete. Wrong = new call for the next train; they pass every 5–10 minutes on weekends, and every train teaches you something.
Outer Mission.where: Cayuga Playground meadow/paths, Cayuga Ave & Naglee Ave, under the BART viaduct.
Outer Mission.photo: The team pointing up at the train mid-count, the viaduct filling the frame.

Outer Mission.title: Find the Edge of San Francisco
Outer Mission.do: Somewhere on Mission Street south of Geneva, San Francisco ends and Daly City begins — and the sidewalk mostly doesn't tell you. Phones away. Walk south and figure out, from clues alone (street-sign styles, house-number jumps, whose trash cans line the curb, any sign you spot), exactly where the city line crosses Mission Street. When the team agrees, plant a shoe on the line and take the photo. Then — and only then — check a map: within one block of the real line = complete. Off = failed; the map has spoiled it.
Outer Mission.where: Mission St, 5000–5900 blocks (Geneva Ave south to the county line).
Outer Mission.photo: A shoe on the guessed line, one teammate on each "side," the map check held up beside it.

Outer Richmond.title: Through the Sutro Tunnel
Outer Richmond.do: Descend to the Sutro Baths ruins (stairs from the Lands End/Merrie Way lot or the trail from Point Lobos Ave). From the interpretive signs, find and report two numbers: how many swimming pools the 1896 bathhouse had (seven — six saltwater, one freshwater) and how many swimmers it held. Then walk the whole team through the rock tunnel at the north end of the ruins to its wave-window openings. Stay on the trail and in the tunnel — never on the wet rocks by the water.
Outer Richmond.where: Sutro Baths ruins, Point Lobos Ave & Merrie Way (below Lands End Lookout).
Outer Richmond.photo: Team silhouetted in the tunnel mouth with the ocean crashing behind — one of the best natural photo frames in San Francisco.

Outer Richmond.title: Dig Your Own Sutro Bath
Outer Richmond.do: Sutro's baths are ruins — build the successor. On the sand at Kelly's Cove (the north end of Ocean Beach, below the Cliff House), dig a pool at least one arm-span across that visibly holds water (carry water up in hands/hats/a bottle — dig on damp sand well above the waterline; nobody enters the surf). Complete when the pool holds standing water with at least one teammate's bare feet in it.
Outer Richmond.where: Ocean Beach at Kelly's Cove — beach access at Balboa St & Great Highway, then walk north toward the Cliff House.
Outer Richmond.photo: Team in swimmer poses around the filled "bath," with the Cliff House headland in the background — your bathhouse, with the real one's cliff behind it.

Outer Richmond.title: The Hidden Huntress
Outer Richmond.do: Enter Sutro Heights Park through the gate flanked by two stone lions (copies of Trafalgar Square's). Phones away: somewhere among the trees is a statue of Diana the Huntress (a concrete copy of the Louvre's Diana, bow in hand) — find her without a map. Then a memory test with three fixed questions: one teammate studies her for 30 seconds, turns their back, and answers (1) which hand holds the bow, (2) which foot is forward, (3) what she is reaching for with her free hand. The team checks against the statue. Three for three = complete; any miss = 30 more seconds, new teammate. Finish at the parapet overlook above the Cliff House.
Outer Richmond.where: Sutro Heights Park, entrance at 48th Ave & Point Lobos Ave. Free, open dawn to dusk.
Outer Richmond.photo: The answerer with their back to Diana mid-answer, then the team at the parapet with the ocean behind.

Pacific Heights.title: The Stair Oracle of Lyon Street
Pacific Heights.do: Pick any one step of the Lyon Street Steps and stand where you can watch it. Before you start, the team agrees on a guess: how many people will set foot on that step in the next five minutes? Write the guess down and photograph it, then start a five-minute timer and count every person (teammates don't count). Complete when your guess is within 3 of the true count (or within 10%, whichever is more generous). Missed? Pick a new number — or a new step — and run another five minutes; you know the traffic now.
Pacific Heights.where: Lyon Street Steps, Lyon St between Green St (bottom) and Broadway (top)
Pacific Heights.photo: The guess note held up next to the final tally, the chosen step behind you, with the Palace of Fine Arts dome and the bay in the distance — bonus points (moral only) for the heart sculpture in the stairway garden if it's in residence.

Pacific Heights.title: Count the Chase Steps
Pacific Heights.do: Alta Plaza Park's grand terraced staircase on the Clay Street side (at Pierce) is the one four cars famously crashed down in the 1972 What's Up, Doc? chase, filmed without permission. Count it: two teammates are the counters. They climb from the sidewalk to the top terrace at the same time, each counting every step silently — no talking, no fingers. At the top, both say their number at the same instant. A match = complete. A mismatch = recount together on the way down and say your numbers again at the bottom. (The chipped step edges the stunt cars left are still there — spotting one is bragging rights, not required.)
Pacific Heights.where: Alta Plaza Park, south stairs at Clay St & Pierce St
Pacific Heights.photo: The two counters holding up matching numbers on the top terrace, downtown skyline behind.

Pacific Heights.title: Cast a Spell at the Witch's House
Pacific Heights.do: Find the gray 1886 Queen Anne Victorian at 2007 Franklin St — the Haas–Lilienthal House, with a corner tower topped by a pointed "witch's cap" roof. Under the turret, hold a spelling bee: one teammate opens any random-word generator on a phone (search "random word generator"), reads the word aloud — and its meaning, if nobody knows it — and the speller casts the spell by spelling it out loud, no peeking. Spelled right = the next teammate steps up with a fresh random word. Spelled wrong = same speller, new word. Complete when every teammate has cast one spell.
Pacific Heights.where: 2007 Franklin St (between Washington & Jackson) — sidewalk only, no tour required
Pacific Heights.photo: The speller mid-incantation under the witch's cap, the word on the phone held up beside them.

Portola.title: The Gate Made of Garden Tools
Portola.do: Enter The Green Between greenway and find artist Dana Albany's 16-foot Gothic metal gate, welded entirely from old tools and hardware. In the gate itself, locate all four of: a hammer, a faucet, a gear, and any garden tool (trowel, shears, rake...). Then walk the greenway until you find the car half-buried nose-down in the ground (a 1969 Dodge Coronet). Complete when you've photographed both.
Portola.where: The Green Between — the greenway strip between San Bruno Ave and the 101 sound wall; enter at the Burrows St end (Burrows St just east of San Bruno Ave).
Portola.photo: Team posed with the half-buried Dodge, plus one shot of a teammate's finger on each of the four objects found in the gate (a 4-tile collage counts).

Portola.title: Garden District Blind Touch
Portola.do: At any market on San Bruno Ave (San Bruno Market, 2480 San Bruno, is the classic), one teammate — the shopper — goes in alone, counts along the produce display, and buys whatever sits in the 3rd, 8th and 13th bins (skip a repeat or anything over $2; take the next bin), $5 total max, keeping them hidden in the bag. Outside, a teammate closes their eyes and is handed the items one at a time: they may touch, squeeze and smell, but not look or taste. Name all three correctly = complete. Any miss = the shopper reshuffles and a new teammate takes the test — one attempt per teammate. When everyone has missed, the shopper buys three new items and the round starts over. Eat the evidence afterward.
Portola.where: San Bruno Ave commercial strip (2400–2600 blocks).
Portola.photo: An eyes-closed teammate mid-squeeze of a mystery vegetable; bonus style if the "Welcome to the Portola — Garden District" sign (San Bruno & Silliman) is behind.

Portola.title: Bottle Flip Under the Marquee
Portola.do: Stand beneath the restored neon marquee of the 1927 Art Deco Avenue Theater — the neighborhood's old movie palace, whose sign (99 pieces of glass) neighbors fought years to relight. Flip a partly-filled water bottle (any size, about a third full) and land it standing upright on the sidewalk. Every teammate must land one. A miss = flip again; unlimited tries.
Portola.photo: The bottle standing, "AVENUE" glowing above it.

Potrero Hill.title: Crookeder Than Lombard?
Potrero Hill.do: Start at the top of Vermont Street's curves at McKinley Square (20th & Vermont, where the "trucks not advised" sign marks the drop). Walk down alongside the switchbacks on the sidewalk — never in the roadway — counting every hairpin turn out loud as a team. Stop at the LAST curve (don't continue to 22nd St under the freeway — that sliver is out of the neighborhood). Completion: proof photo taken, with your official team count held up on fingers. Fun fact to argue on the way down: the Travel Channel measured Vermont's sinuosity at 1.56 vs Lombard's 1.2 — locals say this WPA 1930s street is the real crookedest street in San Francisco.
Potrero Hill.where: Vermont St between 20th St (McKinley Square) and the bottom of the curves, west edge of Potrero Hill
Potrero Hill.photo: Team mid-switchback with fingers showing their hairpin count, the serpentine curves and tree canopy snaking downhill behind them

Potrero Hill.title: State Street Sweep
Potrero Hill.do: Potrero Hill's north–south streets are almost all named for US states. Phones away — no maps. Photograph your team under SIX different state-named street signs (Texas, Missouri, Connecticut, Arkansas, Wisconsin, Carolina, Rhode Island, Kansas, Vermont, Utah, Mississippi, Pennsylvania...). De Haro and San Bruno don't count.
Potrero Hill.where: Along or just off the 18th Street strip.
Potrero Hill.photo: Six state-sign shots; the keeper is the team pointing up at one of them.

Potrero Hill.title: Four Bases in a Row
Potrero Hill.do: At the Potrero Hill Recreation Center ballfield (Arkansas & 22nd), with the downtown skyline behind the outfield, play catch the Little League way: one teammate stands on the pitcher's mound and must throw a ball (bring one, or buy a cheap one on 18th St) to a teammate standing on first, then second, then third, then home — four clean catches in a row. Any drop = start again from first. Team of two: the catcher runs to the next base between throws.
Potrero Hill.where: Potrero Hill Rec Center, 801 Arkansas St (public field; wait out any game in progress).
Potrero Hill.photo: The throw to home, Salesforce Tower standing behind the backstop.

Presidio Heights.title: Dome Peekaboo
Presidio Heights.do: Capture Temple Emanu-El's 150-foot Byzantine dome twice: (a) a close-up from the sidewalk at Lake St and Arguello Blvd with the dome filling the frame and at least one teammate in the shot, and (b) a "peekaboo" shot taken from a spot inside the neighborhood at least 3 blocks away where the dome pokes above rooftops or trees (hunt the westward sightlines along Washington, Jackson, or Clay). Both photos required; the dome must be identifiable in each.
Presidio Heights.where: Temple Emanu-El, Lake St at Arguello Blvd, plus your found vantage point
Presidio Heights.photo: The pair: dome towering overhead up close, then peeking over Presidio Heights rooftops from blocks away.

Presidio Heights.title: Over the Wall, Down the Slide
Presidio Heights.do: At West Pacific Ave and Spruce St, find the old stone Presidio Wall — the boundary that has separated the city from the Army post since the 1890s — and have every teammate touch it. Then pass through into Julius Kahn Playground and every teammate rides the big slide. Completion = all teammates slid.
Presidio Heights.where: Presidio Wall and Julius Kahn Playground, West Pacific Ave at Spruce St
Presidio Heights.photo: The last teammate mid-slide with the rest of the team waving at the bottom.

Presidio Heights.title: Sacramento Street Window Safari
Presidio Heights.do: On Sacramento St between Spruce St and Presidio Ave, photograph 5 different storefront windows, each containing a different item from this list: (1) a chair or lamp, (2) a toy or stuffed animal, (3) fresh flowers or a live plant, (4) an article of clothing, (5) a book or picture frame. One item per storefront, five distinct storefronts, a teammate pointing at the item in every shot. Works from the sidewalk even when the shops are closed.
Presidio Heights.where: Sacramento St, 3300–3700 blocks (Presidio Ave to Spruce St)
Presidio Heights.photo: A five-shot set of teammates pointing out finds in the boutique windows.

Presidio.title: Yoda Paparazzi Count
Presidio.do: Find the Yoda Fountain outside Lucasfilm's headquarters. Before you're close enough to see who's around it, the team agrees on ONE guess: how many people (not counting your team) will take a photo of Yoda in the next TEN minutes? Write it down, then sit on the low wall and count — a phone or camera pointed at the statue counts, each person once. Within 2 of the true count = complete. Off? Call the next ten.
Presidio.where: Yoda Fountain, One Letterman Drive (Letterman Digital Arts Center, just inside the Lombard Gate at Lombard & Lyon). The fountain is outdoors and accessible anytime — don't count on the lobby, which is weekdays-only.
Presidio.photo: The tally sheet held up beside the bronze Yoda, a stranger's camera raised behind.

Presidio.title: Walk the (Wood) Line
Presidio.do: Find Andy Goldsworthy's Wood Line, a 1,200-foot serpentine line of eucalyptus logs snaking through the cypress grove. Each teammate must walk TWENTY consecutive logs without stepping off (arms out for balance — no holding hands). Step off = start your twenty over. Complete when every teammate has done a clean twenty.
Presidio.where: Off Lovers' Lane near Presidio Blvd & W Pacific Ave.
Presidio.photo: The whole team spaced along the curving line, arms out like tightrope walkers.

Presidio.title: Egg Toss at the Outpost
Presidio.do: At the Outpost nature playground at Presidio Tunnel Tops, find the giant wooden bird's nest. Stand ten paces back. Each teammate tosses an "egg" — a tennis ball, a pinecone, a rolled sock — into the nest. Complete when every teammate has landed one inside (unlimited tries). Wait your turn if others are playing in it, and collect every egg after.
Presidio.where: The Outpost at Presidio Tunnel Tops, near the Main Post/Crissy Field overlook. Free; open daily 9:30 AM to 5 PM (6 PM April–October).
Presidio.photo: The egg mid-air over the nest, Tunnel Tops parkland behind.

Russian Hill.title: Walk the Crookedest Street
Russian Hill.do: Walk the famous crooked block of Lombard Street from top (Hyde) to bottom (Leavenworth) on the sidewalk stairs. That's it — the street is the challenge.
Russian Hill.where: Lombard St, 1000 block, between Hyde St and Leavenworth St.
Russian Hill.photo: The team at the bottom with the brick switchbacks and hydrangeas rising behind.

Russian Hill.title: Postcard Ambush
Russian Hill.do: Recreate SF's most famous postcard, live: ONE photo containing a moving Powell–Hyde cable car, the Bay with Alcatraz behind it, and at least one teammate. Stake out your angle and time the shot; if a car passes and you miss, wait for the next one (roughly every 10 minutes on weekends).
Russian Hill.where: Hyde St between Lombard and Bay (Hyde & Greenwich or Hyde & Lombard crests give the Alcatraz backdrop).
Russian Hill.photo: The proof IS the challenge: cable car + Alcatraz + teammate in one frame.

Russian Hill.title: Stand Up Straight on the 31.5%
Russian Hill.do: Filbert Street between Leavenworth and Hyde is one of the steepest blocks in San Francisco. On a SLOPED part of the sidewalk (not a flat stair tread), build something at least ONE FOOT tall that stands truly upright — plumb to gravity, not tilted with the hill. Use anything you're carrying, find, or buy nearby (up to $10). It must stand on its own for a count of ten with no hands touching it, and a phone level app held against it must read within 5° of vertical. Falls or leans too far? Rebuild and try again.
Russian Hill.where: Filbert St between Leavenworth St and Hyde St (sidewalk only; keep everything off the roadway). Shops for supplies along Hyde St a block or two south and on Polk St a few blocks west.
Russian Hill.photo: The tower standing dead vertical against the plunging street, level app reading shown, team hands in the air.

Seacliff.title: Junk Boat Shipyard
Seacliff.do: On the sand at China Beach, build a model junk (Chinese sailing boat) at least 12 inches long from found beach materials only (driftwood, kelp, stones, feathers — nothing brought with you). It must have a hull and at least one standing "sail." Complete when the finished boat stands on its own on the sand.
Seacliff.where: China Beach, down the stairway/drive at the seaward end of Sea Cliff Avenue
Seacliff.photo: The finished junk on the sand with the Golden Gate Bridge in the background

Seacliff.title: The Fishermen's Stone, From Memory
Seacliff.do: Find the 1981 memorial stone at the top of the China Beach access drive honoring the Chinese fishermen who camped in the cove since Gold Rush times. One teammate, the scribe, studies the four Chinese characters on it for 30 seconds — no photos — then walks twenty paces away, turns their back, and draws all four from memory on paper or a phone. The team holds the drawing up to the stone: all four recognizably right, every stroke group present = complete. Anything missing = another 30-second look, new scribe.
Seacliff.where: Seaward end of Sea Cliff Avenue, beside the China Beach entrance/parking
Seacliff.photo: The drawing held up beside the carved characters on the stone.

Seacliff.title: The Only Avenue With a Compass
Seacliff.do: Phones away, no maps. Somewhere within three blocks of the China Beach gate is the only numbered avenue in San Francisco whose name carries a compass direction. Find its street sign by walking and reading signs — no asking. Complete when the whole team is under the sign and someone reads it aloud on video.
Seacliff.where: Sea Cliff, within three blocks of Sea Cliff Ave & 28th Ave (the answer is on the map; the challenge is finding it without one)
Seacliff.photo: The team under the sign that gives it away.

South of Market.title: Ride the 1906 Survivor
South of Market.do: Buy carousel tickets ($3/rider) and ride a full cycle of the LeRoy King Carousel — the hand-carved 1906 Charles Looff carousel that once spun at Playland at the Beach. At least two teammates must ride (riders under 42" need a paying companion). Complete when the ride ends.
South of Market.where: Children's Creativity Museum carousel pavilion, 701 Howard St at 4th (Yerba Buena Gardens). Weekends 10am–4pm — no museum admission needed for the carousel.
South of Market.photo: Teammates mid-spin on their carved animals, organ pipes and painted menagerie in frame.

South of Market.title: Call It at the Mint
South of Market.do: Stand on the 5th Street steps (or Mint Plaza side) of the Old Mint — the 1874 "Granite Lady" that survived the 1906 earthquake and fire while holding roughly a third of the nation's gold reserve. Flip a coin and call it in the air; complete the challenge by calling it correctly 5 times IN A ROW. A miss resets the streak — keep flipping until you hit it. Bring your own quarter.
South of Market.where: Old San Francisco Mint, 88 5th St at Mission; Mint Plaza is the quieter flank.
South of Market.photo: The winning flip: coin on palm, granite columns of the Mint rising behind.

South of Market.title: Behind the Waterfall
South of Market.do: Find the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial and walk the passage BEHIND its 50-foot curtain of falling water. The glass panels there carry Dr. King's words in many languages, honoring SF's sister cities — several aren't in the Latin alphabet. Phones away: no translation apps, no searching, no asking. As a team, identify FIVE of the panels' languages by name, and commit to all five in one photographed list before checking anything. Then verify (panels are captioned, or check afterward). All five right = complete. Any wrong = failed. One shot.
South of Market.where: Yerba Buena Gardens, 750 Howard St side of the Great Lawn, between 3rd and 4th. Gardens open 6am–10pm daily, free.
South of Market.photo: The team's written list of five languages held up in front of the panels, sheet of water blurring behind.

Sunset/Parkside.title: Bigger Than Your Biggest Teammate
Sunset/Parkside.do: On the sand at Ocean Beach (between Lincoln Way and Sloat Blvd), write your team name — or team color, if the name is long — in letters drawn in the sand, each letter TALLER than your tallest teammate. To prove scale, that teammate lies down in the sand next to one letter. Complete when the photo shows every letter plus the human yardstick.
Sunset/Parkside.where: Ocean Beach, easiest access from the Judah, Noriega, or Taraval stairwells off the old Great Highway
Sunset/Parkside.photo: Shot from the seawall/dune above: giant sand letters with a teammate lying beside one for scale, ocean behind

Sunset/Parkside.title: Spin the Wheel of Fortune at Polly Ann
Sunset/Parkside.do: At Polly Ann Ice Cream (scooping on Noriega since 1955), ask the counter to spin their famous flavor Wheel of Fortune. One player buys a single scoop of whatever flavor the wheel lands on — durian included — and takes at least three bites. Complete when the wheel's flavor is bought and bitten.
Sunset/Parkside.where: Polly Ann Ice Cream, 3142 Noriega St at 39th Ave (open daily from late morning)
Sunset/Parkside.photo: The spinner mid-lick of the mystery flavor, pointing at the wheel behind the counter

Sunset/Parkside.title: The Doelger Rainbow
Sunset/Parkside.do: The Sunset is the world's biggest showcase of identical pastel stucco rowhouses. Find one block face where FIVE consecutive attached houses are each painted a clearly different color, and line your whole team up in front of them, one player per house. Complete when the photo shows five adjacent, five-colored facades.
Sunset/Parkside.where: Anywhere in the avenues — the blocks between Irving and Vicente from ~30th to 47th Ave are prime hunting ground
Sunset/Parkside.photo: Five teammates (or fewer, spread out) each fronting a different-colored house in an unbroken pastel row

Tenderloin.title: The Six-Dollar Legend
Tenderloin.do: Buy one banh mi at Saigon Sandwich (560 Larkin St at Eddy) — or, if the line is out the door, at any other banh mi counter on Larkin between Turk and O'Farrell. Every teammate takes at least one bite. Complete when the sandwich is bought and everyone has bitten.
Tenderloin.where: Larkin St, Eddy to O'Farrell (officially designated Little Saigon); Saigon Sandwich is open daily, weekends from 7am
Tenderloin.photo: The whole team mid-bite on the Larkin sidewalk, Vietnamese storefront signage behind.

Tenderloin.title: Blade Sign Alphabet
Tenderloin.do: The Uptown Tenderloin Historic District keeps the West's densest collection of century-old hotel signs. Photograph five vintage hotel signs — neon blades or painted ghost signs, five different buildings — whose hotel names begin with FIVE DIFFERENT letters. No phone research or maps; eyes up, feet moving. Complete at the fifth letter.
Tenderloin.where: Richest hunting along Geary, O'Farrell, and Eddy between Larkin and Taylor; the Cadillac Hotel (398 Eddy) is a classic opener
Tenderloin.photo: Sign #5 with a teammate pointing up, plus the full five-letter set in the upload.

Tenderloin.title: The Catalog Is You
Tenderloin.do: Enter the Main Library (free, everyone welcome). From the door: all phones away, no catalog computers, no asking staff. Find a physical copy of Armistead Maupin's Tales of the City on the open shelves — any edition, and any volume of the series counts — using nothing but floor directories, shelf signage, and your own logic. Complete when a teammate is holding the book. (No copy on the shelf after an honest search of the right section? Any book by Maupin counts.)
Tenderloin.where: SF Main Library, 100 Larkin St at Grove — one block from UN Plaza (weekends roughly 10–6 Sat, 12–6 Sun; check hours)
Tenderloin.photo: The book held aloft under the library's 75-foot atrium skylight.

Treasure Island.title: Touch the Sky at the Point of Infinity
Treasure Island.do: Get to Panorama Park on Yerba Buena Island, home of the 69-foot "Point of Infinity" spire. Find the one spot on the hilltop where, in a single photo, the spire's tip appears to touch exactly the top of Salesforce Tower (or the Transamerica Pyramid's spire) across the bay — two points meeting, no gap, no overlap. Complete when the photo shows the two tips kissing. (The Muni 25 stops on Yerba Buena Island on its loop, or it's a ~12-minute uphill walk from the Treasure Island flats — an easy paved climb.)
Treasure Island.where: Panorama Park, hilltop of Yerba Buena Island (opened 2024, free, open daily)
Treasure Island.photo: The two tips meeting — a 69-foot needle and a 1,070-foot tower, joined.

Treasure Island.title: Skyline Roll Call
Treasure Island.do: From the western-shore seawall walkway along Avenue of the Palms, spot and photograph (zoom is fine) 4 of these 5 landmarks: the Transamerica Pyramid, Salesforce Tower, Coit Tower, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate Bridge. Complete when you have all four in photos taken from the seawall (one wide labeled shot or four zoomed shots both count).
Treasure Island.where: Western shore of Treasure Island, seawall along Avenue of the Palms (any point between Building One and the Great Lawn)
Treasure Island.photo: The full postcard panorama with the team in front — the exact view the 1939 fair was built to show off

Treasure Island.title: Paper Clipper Airfield
Treasure Island.do: In the 1930s, Pan Am's China Clipper flying boats took off from Clipper Cove. Fold one paper airplane per teammate (bring paper). From a marked line at Clipper Cove's beach or lawn, each teammate throws; the challenge is complete when any plane flies at least 8 walking paces before touching down. You get 3 rounds of throws total. Retrieve every plane — leave no paper behind.
Treasure Island.where: Clipper Cove Beach / marina shoreline, between Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island (off Treasure Island Road at the causeway)
Treasure Island.photo: A plane mid-launch over the cove, Bay Bridge in the background

Twin Peaks.title: Semaphore on the Twins
Twin Peaks.do: Split your team in two. One group climbs the stair-path to the top of Eureka Peak (north), the other to Noe Peak (south) — they're only ~660 feet apart across the saddle. The Noe group generates a random letter (any random-letter site) and forms it with their bodies (arms, legs, one person or a pile of people — a Y, a T, an X, a 7...). The Eureka group reads it across the gap and texts ONE answer. Right = swap: Eureka forms one, Noe reads it. Complete when both peaks have read one correctly. Wrong = new letter. Team of two: one person per peak, one letter each.
Twin Peaks.where: Eureka and Noe summit paths off Twin Peaks Blvd, uphill from the Christmas Tree Point parking area.
Twin Peaks.photo: Zoomed from one summit: the other half of the team spelling their letter against the sky.

Twin Peaks.title: Bridge or No Bridge?
Twin Peaks.do: Before anyone can see north — standing in the Christmas Tree Point parking area facing the hillside — the team writes one word on a phone screen: "BRIDGE" or "NO BRIDGE," predicting whether at least one Golden Gate Bridge tower will be visible when you reach the Eureka Peak summit. Photograph the written call, then climb. You win only if reality matches your call at the moment you summit. One shot, no take-backs.
Twin Peaks.where: Christmas Tree Point lot (call), Eureka Peak summit (verdict).
Twin Peaks.photo: Two-photo proof: the pre-climb phone screen with the call, then the summit panorama toward the Golden Gate showing bridge or fog — team pointing either way.

Twin Peaks.title: The Market Street Arrow
