Twin Peaks.do: From the Christmas Tree Point overlook, find the one spot where Market Street runs as a single straight line from the bottom of your frame all the way to the bay, and photograph it — the street must be readable as one continuous stripe pointing at the Ferry Building/waterfront. If the fog has eaten downtown, you may mark this failed and re-attempt any time you're back in the neighborhood.
Twin Peaks.where: Christmas Tree Point overlook railing, just below Eureka Peak.
Twin Peaks.photo: The classic postcard nobody frames right: Market Street as a perfect arrow from your feet to the water.

Lone Mountain/USF.title: Conquer the Spanish Steps of the West
Lone Mountain/USF.do: Climb the Lone Mountain grand staircase from Turk Boulevard to the top — every teammate, no shortcuts. Pick two counters; each silently counts the steps on the way up. At the top, both write their number down hidden and reveal together. The counts must MATCH. Mismatch = walk back down and recount on the next climb. At the mid-landing, everyone roars at the gilded lion's-head spout of the Alessandri Fountain.
Lone Mountain/USF.where: Lone Mountain grand staircase, from Turk Blvd up to the top terrace.
Lone Mountain/USF.photo: The two matching numbers held up at the top terrace, the city behind.

Lone Mountain/USF.title: Pinch a Spire
Lone Mountain/USF.do: St. Ignatius Church's twin spires rise 210 feet and once guided ships into the Bay. Take a forced-perspective photo in which one teammate appears to pinch the tip of a spire between thumb and forefinger — the pinch must look convincing (fingers visually touching the spire tip), and BOTH towers must be in the frame. Complete when you have the shot.
Lone Mountain/USF.where: Sidewalks around St. Ignatius Church, Fulton St & Parker Ave (the Fulton Street side and the lawn edges give the best angles).
Lone Mountain/USF.photo: The forced-perspective spire pinch with both towers of the giant church.

Lone Mountain/USF.title: Walk Through the 1500s
Lone Mountain/USF.do: USF's Kalmanovitz Hall is framed by two genuinely ancient doorways shipped from Europe: the Santa Maria de Ovila Portal (1575, from a Spanish monastery — it frames the outdoor auditorium stage) and a Romanesque portal from 12th–13th century northern Italy carved with Adam and Eve. Find both. One teammate stands framed inside the 1575 archway; at the older portal, a teammate points directly at the Adam and Eve carving. Complete when both photos are taken.
Lone Mountain/USF.where: Kalmanovitz Hall and its outdoor terraces, USF main campus (uphill from Fulton St near Parker Ave).
Lone Mountain/USF.photo: Teammate posed in a 450-year-old stone archway; teammate pointing at an 800-year-old Adam and Eve.

Visitacion Valley.title: Climb the Garden Ladder
Visitacion Valley.do: The Visitacion Valley Greenway is a ladder of six block-long gardens. Start at Hans Schiller Plaza on Leland Ave and climb one garden at a time — crossing Raymond, Arleta, Teddy, Campbell and Tucker — to the Native Plant Garden at Tioga Ave. At each garden, spot one decorative ironwork detail (animal, plant, or vegetable) worked into its gate or fence. At the top, a chosen teammate must recite all six details in order, bottom to top, from memory. Mistake = start the recital over (you may walk back down to re-check). Gardens may be locked; the gates and fences are on the public sidewalk.
Visitacion Valley.where: Visitacion Valley Greenway, Leland Ave up to Tioga Ave.
Visitacion Valley.photo: The reciter at the top garden, eyes closed, counting off six fingers.

Visitacion Valley.title: Count the Keys
Visitacion Valley.do: In front of the 1926 brick Schlage Lock office building — sole survivor of the lock factory that ran Vis Valley's economy for 70 years — every teammate secretly writes down a guess: how many keys is the WHOLE team carrying right now? No peeking in pockets. Then everyone empties their keys into a pile and you count (a fob or car key counts as one). Anyone within 2 of the true count = complete. Nobody within 2 = failed. One count, ever.
Visitacion Valley.where: Schlage Lock building, Bayshore Blvd near Blanken Ave.
Visitacion Valley.photo: The pile of keys on the sidewalk, the winning guess held above it, the brick building behind.

Visitacion Valley.title: Silent Movie in Little Hollywood
Visitacion Valley.do: Go to Little Hollywood Park in the 1920s storybook enclave named for its movie-set houses, and shoot a silent movie: one teammate, the director, generates a random number 1–10 on a phone and whispers that scene to the actor — 1 brushing teeth, 2 walking a dog, 3 making a sandwich, 4 catching a fish, 5 changing a tire, 6 parallel parking, 7 milking a cow, 8 flying a kite, 9 shoveling snow, 10 juggling (re-roll repeats). The actor performs it with no sound and no props. The rest of the team gets ONE guess. Right = new actor, new scene. Wrong = the streak restarts. Complete when the team guesses three scenes in a row.
Visitacion Valley.where: Little Hollywood Park, Lathrop Ave & Tocoloma Ave (east of Bayshore Blvd)
Visitacion Valley.photo: The actor mid-scene on the lawn, the storybook cottages behind.

West of Twin Peaks.title: Summit the Hidden Cross
West of Twin Peaks.do: Enter Mount Davidson Park from Juanita Way or Dalewood Way and follow the forest trail to the summit — a gentle 10-minute walk under the eucalyptus. The 103-foot concrete cross (lit by FDR himself via telegraph in 1934, and rumored to be 3 feet taller than planned because the crew had leftover concrete) stays invisible in the fog-forest until you step into the clearing. Every teammate must touch the cross at the same time, AND you must find the Armenian Genocide memorial plaque at its base. Complete when both photos are taken.
West of Twin Peaks.where: Mount Davidson Park summit; trailheads at Juanita Way (north) or Dalewood Way (southwest).
West of Twin Peaks.photo: Low-angle shot from the cross's base: the whole team, palms on the concrete, with all 103 feet towering out of frame above them — taken at the highest natural point in San Francisco.

West of Twin Peaks.title: Tunnel Roulette
West of Twin Peaks.do: Stand on the West Portal Ave sidewalk with a clear view of the ornate 1918 Twin Peaks Tunnel mouth. Three streetcar lines — K, L, and M — all pop out of that one hole. Start a video and call ONE letter out loud BEFORE the next outbound train's headlights appear in the tunnel. If the train that emerges shows your letter: done. If not: failed, forever. (A shuttle or out-of-service train doesn't count — redo the call.)
West of Twin Peaks.where: Twin Peaks Tunnel west portal, West Portal Ave at Ulloa St.
West of Twin Peaks.photo: Video freeze-frame or photo of the team pointing at the emerging train, its route letter legible — triumph or agony, both are keepers.

West of Twin Peaks.title: Exact Change at Shaw's
West of Twin Peaks.do: Shaw's has sold candy on this block since 1931. As a team, choose candy whose prices add up to EXACTLY $5.00 before any tax — no more, no less. No phone calculators; mental math and paper only. Ring it up: exactly $5.00 = complete. Off? Back to the shelves, re-add on paper, and try again — three register trips maximum, then it's failed.
West of Twin Peaks.where: Shaw's, 122 West Portal Ave. (If Shaw's is closed, any West Portal sweet shop counts.)
West of Twin Peaks.photo: The receipt reading $5.00 held up with the candy haul, Shaw's sign behind.

Western Addition.title: Marquee Charades
Western Addition.do: Stand under the Fillmore Auditorium's corner marquee and read off the show names posted there and on the building's poster cases (if fewer than five names are up, add names from the venue's own upcoming-shows list on your phone until you have at least five written down). Number the list. One teammate is the headliner: they generate a random number on a phone (re-roll repeats), keep it secret, and act that name out, no words, no letters, no pointing at the sign. The team gets ONE guess. Right = the next teammate headlines with a fresh name. Wrong = new name, and the streak resets. Complete when the team gets three names in a row.
Western Addition.where: The Fillmore, 1805 Geary Blvd at Fillmore St, southwest corner (exterior only).
Western Addition.photo: The headliner frozen mid-act with the marquee readable above them, the rest of the team mid-shout.

Western Addition.title: Fourteen Tiers of Silence
Western Addition.do: Go inside St. Mary's Cathedral (free, open daily until 5 p.m., later on Saturdays; if a Mass is underway, play from the back in silence) and stand under the altar canopy: a one-ton curtain of thousands of aluminum rods hung on gold wire. Two teammates are the counters. On "go," each silently counts how many horizontal tiers of rods the canopy has, top to bottom — no talking, no pointing, no fingers until the end. When both are done, they hold up their numbers at the same instant. Match = complete. Mismatch = both counters walk once around the nave, come back, and recount.
Western Addition.where: Cathedral of St. Mary of the Assumption, 1111 Gough St at Geary Blvd, Cathedral Hill (enter from the plaza; visitors welcome outside service times).
Western Addition.photo: The two counters holding up matching numbers, the glittering canopy and the four colored window ribbons of the roof cross behind them.

Western Addition.title: Taboo on the Blue Bridge
Western Addition.do: Walk out on the Fillmore St bridge over the Geary trench and find the 20 blue glass panels etched with a jazz poem (an installation called Three Shades of Blue). Number the panels 1–20 in your head from the Fillmore-Auditorium end. One teammate is the describer: they secretly pick a panel, read it, and describe what it says in their own words — none of the words on the glass, no numbers, no spelling. The team reads along the bridge and points at ONE panel. Right = new describer, new panel. Wrong = same describer, new panel, streak resets. Complete at three in a row. Tip: the etching is faint; read it with the light behind you, up close.
Western Addition.where: Fillmore St bridge over Geary Blvd, between the Fillmore (1805 Geary) and the north side; stay on the sidewalk side of the panels.
Western Addition.photo: The describer mid-gesture with the team pointing at a blue panel, the Geary trench and the 38 buses below.
